title_clean: Samānamaṇḍikāputta Sutta (MN 78): The Ten Qualities of the Accomplished
description_short: Bhante explores the ten qualities that define a truly accomplished practitioner, contrasting superficial virtue with genuine liberation through the Eightfold Path.
description_long:
In this teaching on the Samānamaṇḍikāputta Sutta (MN 78), Bhante Bodhidhamma introduces us to Pañcakaṅga, King Pasenadi's carpenter, who encounters different views on spiritual accomplishment. The Buddha masterfully corrects the simplistic understanding that avoiding evil actions alone constitutes liberation, using the memorable example of an infant to illustrate this point.

The discourse reveals the ten essential qualities of one who is truly 'accomplished in what is wholesome': the complete Eightfold Path plus right knowledge (sammā ñāṇa) and right deliverance (sammā vimutti). Bhante explains how unwholesome and wholesome mental habits originate from the heart-mind (citta) and perceptions respectively, and how both ultimately cease without remainder in the Arahant through the Four Right Efforts.

Particularly illuminating is the teaching on how even wholesome actions contain traces of self-identification until complete awakening, when actions become purely functional (kriyā). This sutta provides essential understanding of the progression from ordinary virtue through jhānic states to final liberation, making it invaluable for serious practitioners seeking to understand the complete path to awakening.
